articles.headline: Editorial items: Theodore Tilton's lecture before the S. C. S. Association; reception at William Still's
articles.summary: Theodore Tilton. This distinguished gentleman lectured before the S. C. S. Association (a colored organization) to an immense audience on Monday evening last at Concert Hall, subject 'Reconstruction.' His doctrine was 'both pure and sound' and enunciated with his marvellous power. Mr. Tilton was the guest of our fellow townsman, William Still, who gave a reception, after the lecture, in his honor, which was attended by a number of ladies and gentlemen.

events.name: Bethel A.M.E. Church and the M. W. Grand Lodge A. Y. M. of Pennsylvania -- exchange of presentations
events.location: Philadelphia (Bethel A.M.E. Church and the Grand Lodge)
events.description: Quite recently the M. W. Grand Lodge A. Y. M. for the State of Pennsylvania presented to Bethel A.M.E. Church a handsome silver Communion Service. On Tuesday, March 26th, the Trustees and Stewards of Bethel Church made a return presentation to the Grand Lodge, consisting of a handsome Bible, Gavel, and silver Square and Compass, with a written declaration of Christian friendship, enclosed in a beautifully carved walnut frame, bearing the signature of the Pastor, Rev. J. Hollen, the Treasurer, Rev. S. Smith, the Secretary, Mr. L. R. Seymour, and those of the Trustees and Stewards. The design and execution of the Declaration was by the artist Mr. W. B. Jones, of 616 Pine St. The testimonial was presented by Mr. Abram Flrid [VERIFY; probably Field], and received by Rev. Theo. D. Miller, G. C. Addresses were also delivered by Rev. Jas. Lynch, Nathaniel L. Durham, W. G. M., and others.

events.name: Central Presbyterian Church Sabbath-school -- anniversary
events.description: The Anniversary of the Sabbath-school of the Central Presbyterian Church was held on Wednesday evening of last week (Mar 27). Recitations, dialogues and singing before a large audience. Mr. J. L. Freeman, the musical conductor, was ably assisted by Misses Davis and McKee. 'Household Economy', a dialogue, was well rendered by two scholars. A poem, 'The Return of the Regiment', was recited by Miss Julia Jones. A recitation [?], 'The Wind and Harp', merited much praise. The singing of the choruses by the school was excellent.
attendees: scholar, recited 'The Return of the Regiment' (Miss)

events.name: Union baptism by immersion of thirty-three converts of the Philadelphia A.M.E. churches at the Delaware River
events.location: Zion Mission Church, thence to the Delaware River at the foot of Moore street, Philadelphia
events.description: Editorial 'Baptism': The several A.M.E. churches of this city recently made large accessions to their membership; thirty-three among them who had not been baptized in infancy desired to be immersed. The pastors, Revs. Hollen, Gibbs, Gould and Watson, arranged a Union Baptism, which took place in the southern part of the city at the Delaware River on last Sabbath morning (April 14) at nine o'clock. They met at the Zion Mission church about eight o'clock A.M., where the preliminary exercises were conducted by Rev. Theo. Gould, and from thence proceeded to the foot of Moore street. The solemn rite was administered by Elder Theodore Gould, assisted by Deacons Thomas Jones and William G. Cooper. An immense concourse of people behaved in an orderly manner; 'the old citizens say that no similar occasion for many years past created greater interest.' (Procession from church to river: parades/processions topic.)
attendees: elder, administered the baptism (printed 'Theo. Gould', 'Theodore Gould')

events.name: Zion Mission A.M.E. Church -- love feast, twenty-six received into full membership
events.description: A.M.E. Items, Philadelphia: The Love-feast at Zion Mission A.M.E. Church on last Monday evening was a Love-feast indeed; the house was well filled. Rev. T. Gould, the pastor, received into full membership twenty-six persons; about twenty still remain on probation.

Burris on Monday evening, April 29th, 1867 at Liberty Hall, by the members of the Delmonico Band; vocalists Miss Fey [?], Miss Deaver [?] and Miss Shay [?]. Leader of the band, Mr. Boyer; conductor, Prof. Wm. H. Davis; vocal conductor, Mr. Freeman; pianist, Miss A. E. Burris.
